name: The Altered Velvet Band
oneSentenceBio: The Altered Velvet Band turns soul, blues, brass-band energy, funk, ska, and communal rhythm into living music that invites everyone into the room.
threeSentenceBio: The Altered Velvet Band celebrates American communal music as something active, physical, and shared. Brass, rhythm, voice, and groove converse across soul, blues, funk, Louisiana traditions, and ska without settling for generic retro styling. The music feels warm, local, and alive - built for dancing, call-and-response, crowded rooms, and the moment an audience becomes part of the band. Ensemble interplay and human momentum keep every tradition moving forward rather than preserving it behind glass.
paragraphBio: The Altered Velvet Band makes music that feels shared before the first chorus is over. Brass answers the voice, the rhythm section pushes the room forward, and grooves draw from Memphis soul, Chicago blues, Louisiana jazz, funk, ska, and dance-floor traditions without reducing any of them to costume. The project is interested in the living social force of these sounds: musicians listening to one another, a crowd responding in real time, and a song becoming larger because everyone in the room has entered it. Arrangements favor ensemble conversation and human momentum over sterile perfection. Horns can shout, vocals can testify, and the groove should feel capable of spilling out of the venue and into the street. The Altered Velvet Band respects the source traditions that make this music possible, but it does not aim for museum-piece recreation. It brings their warmth, swagger, joy, and communal urgency into the present. This is music for dancing, parades, block parties, clubs, festivals, and anyone who believes the line between audience and performer should sometimes disappear.
